summary.text: Niki Conforti is the Republican nominee for Illinois' 6th District and an energy consultant from Glen Ellyn.
She worked for years in healthcare administration and owned a staffing business, and she is seeking a rematch with Democratic Rep. Sean Casten, who defeated her in 2024.

paragraphs.text: According to her campaign website, Conforti is a lifelong resident of Chicago's western suburbs, a single mother and a member of a family of military veterans.
She grew up in a family-owned business and later owned her own staffing business.
She graduated from the University of Chicago School of Economics and earned an M.B.A. in healthcare administration from George Washington University.
Conforti spent about 12 years on the administration side of large health systems, including as a director, and says she wrote corporate policy there.
She now works as an energy consultant; WTTW's voter guide lists that as her occupation since 2017.
According to her campaign website, she has been involved in philanthropic efforts through her church and with International Orthodox Christian Charities and Mothers2Mothers.
Conforti first ran for this seat in 2022, finishing third in the June Republican primary with 11.4% of the vote; Keith Pekau won the nomination.
She won the March 2024 Republican primary and lost the November general election to Sean Casten, 54.2% to 45.8%.
On March 17, 2026, she won the Republican primary with 82.2% of the vote over Skylar Duensing, setting up a November rematch with Casten.
